title: Pattern machine
subtitle: Find the rule before predicting the next value.
learning_objective: Recognise and extend an additive number pattern.

sections.heading: Look for a consistent change
sections.body: Compare neighbouring terms. A pattern rule must explain every step, not just the first two numbers.

sections.reasoning: Checking every gap confirms the rule.

sections.heading: Check twice
sections.body: Use your rule on two different steps before extending a sequence.

sections.heading: Explain the rule
sections.body: State both the starting value and the repeated change.

title: Pattern detective
subtitle: Describe a rule with clear mathematical language.
learning_objective: Explain how a number sequence changes.

sections.heading: Name the operation
sections.body: A useful rule states the starting value and the operation repeated at each step.

sections.heading: A reliable method
steps: Test the same operation across the sequence.

sections.heading: Verify
sections.body: Apply the stated rule to each pair of neighbouring terms.

title: Factor arrays
subtitle: Use equal rows to reveal factor pairs.

sections.heading: Factors make complete groups
sections.body: A factor divides a number into equal groups with no remainder. Each rectangular array gives a factor pair.

sections.heading: Factor or multiple?
sections.body: Factors divide the number; multiples are produced by multiplying the number.

sections.heading: Pair check
sections.body: Reverse each factor pair to confirm it describes the same array.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.prompt: Which is a factor pair of 20?

title: Common multiple paths
subtitle: Compare skip-counting paths to find a meeting point.
learning_objective: Identify common multiples of two numbers.

sections.heading: Two lists can meet
sections.body: Write multiples in order. A common multiple appears in both lists; the least common multiple is the first positive meeting point.

sections.problem: Find the least common multiple of 3 and 4.

sections.heading: Stop at the first match
sections.body: Ordered lists make the least common multiple visible without guessing.

sections.heading: Why least?
sections.body: Confirm that no smaller positive value appears in both lists.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.prompt: What is the least common multiple of 5 and 3?
sections.hint: List a few multiples of each.
